checks.name: Queue identity
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test interaction queue_identity::
checks.output: 10 tests pass. The five request kinds (Steer, Retry, Reorder, Cancel, Undo) are not interchangeable -- assigning a CancelRequest to a SteerRequest is a doctest compile_fail, and so is assigning a String to a SteerRequest. A queued item carries its own opaque identity and session reference rather than an in-memory prompt string, and an item cannot be smuggled into another session's queue. Empty, over-bound and duplicate-identity queues each fail with their own category; appending assigns the next position and refuses a repeated identity; position arithmetic is checked with no wrapping successor. Reorder preserves exactly the identities the receiver held, cannot invent one or address a slot that is not there, the last rank is addressable and the next one is refused, and a destination is a rank in the current order rather than a stored position.

checks.name: Attempt lineage
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test interaction attempt_lineage::
checks.output: 3 tests pass: a retry names its immediate predecessor and the original attempt, a retry of a retry records both references rather than collapsing to one, and no constructor addresses or mutates prior evidence -- a retry produces a successor attempt intent and has no parameter naming an evidence record.

checks.name: Idempotent intents
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test interaction idempotent_intents:: review_regressions::
checks.output: 4 + 2 tests pass. A repeated stop and a repeated undo each yield one typed outcome and one effect; idempotency is keyed by request identity rather than by request shape, and the regression tests confirm that reusing one request identity for a different request is reported as a collision rather than silently treated as a replay. An irreversible undo target fails with its own category instead of succeeding silently.

checks.name: Checkpoint identity
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test interaction checkpoint_identity:: && rustc --edition 2024 --emit=metadata --extern automonique_protocol=rust/target/debug/libautomonique_protocol.rlib -L dependency=rust/target/debug/deps - (RestoreCheckpoint::latest())
checks.output: 4 tests pass: create, list and restore are distinct typed operations, a restore requires the exact content digest and revision, a digest identifies at most one restore point, and an unknown target fails. I compiled `RestoreCheckpoint::latest()` and rustc rejected it with error[E0599] (no function named latest), so an unqualified restore is unrepresentable and that compile_fail fails for its intended reason; passing a CreateCheckpoint to restore is a second compile_fail in the doc suite.

checks.name: Compression lineage
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test interaction compression_lineage:: && rustc --edition 2024 --emit=metadata ... - (entry.digest = ...)
checks.output: 9 tests pass: every lineage component is recorded (source range, compressor provider and model identity, prompt/template digest, output digest, protected facts, verification status), a missing or over-bound component is refused, an over-long or control-bearing component is refused, the range needs both endpoints and may not run backwards but may cover exactly one revision, a range the transcript does not hold is refused, verification status is explicit rather than inferred from absence, and a compression is a derived view that never replaces an authoritative entry at its own revision. I compiled a direct field write `entry.digest = ContentDigest::new("sha256:rewritten")` and rustc rejected it with error[E0616] (private field), so no value can express a transcript rewrite.

checks.name: Context usage
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test interaction context_usage::
checks.output: 4 tests pass. ContextComponentClass::ALL has exactly 8 members with distinct spellings and a stable index order, lookup answers for the class asked about, a breakdown missing a class fails with missing_component_class naming it and a repeated class fails with duplicate_component_class. Estimated and provider-reported counts are independently nullable across all four combinations; a null provider count carries one of the typed MissingCountReason values, reports None for its token count against a positive control that reads back 4242 when the provider did report it, and the estimate stays on its own side -- the reported total for a breakdown with one unreported class is 7*20 and that class is named in `unreported()` rather than filled in from its 1000-token estimate. Assigning an EstimatedTokens into the provider-reported slot is a doctest compile_fail.

checks.name: Projection authority
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test interaction projection_authority:: quality:: && rustc --edition 2024 --emit=metadata ... - (projection.set_surface(...) and an AuthorizedIntent struct literal)
checks.output: 5 + 4 tests pass. A projection exposes observed state and changes none of it, every action it offers names the authority it requires, a presentation shortcut is not a new authority, a namespaced projection cannot name, read or address another extension's namespace, and one command vocabulary serves every surface with no per-surface parsing. I compiled two escapes: `projection.set_surface(SurfaceKind::Cli)` was rejected with error[E0599] (no such method) and an `AuthorizedIntent { .. }` struct literal was rejected with error[E0451] (private fields), so a shortcut cannot fabricate an authority. `CommandInvocation::parse("/undo")` is a further doctest compile_fail: there is no per-surface parser, alias table or regular expression in the value layer. The quality module additionally checks that every published byte bound and collection bound is the edge a real rejection uses and that every published error category is reachable and distinct.
